question: What is dinner table syndrome?
description: Dinner table syndrome is a deaf or hard of hearing person being left out while a group talks around them, most often at a family meal.
In the Rochester Deaf Health Survey of 211 deaf adults, in PLOS ONE, 80.6% of those with hearing parents recalled following family talk only sometimes or never as children.
Researchers in PLOS ONE call dinner table syndrome a catch-all phrase for a commonly experienced phenomenon in the Deaf community.
More than 90% of deaf children in the US are born to hearing parents, according to the NIDCD.
In any group conversation, Hearing Dogs for Deaf People advises taking turns to talk and keeping faces out of shadow.
RNID reported in 2025 that 54% of people who are deaf or have hearing loss have been told it doesn't matter after asking for a repeat.
Captio AI is a live captions app made for deaf and hard of hearing people, and it shows speaker labels when a phone sits in the middle of the table.
Captio AI is one tool among others and does not replace sign language or people taking turns at the table.
